python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Data from December 1941 to December 1942 (from table element 281)
# Bonds = interest-bearing bonds
# Bills and certificates of indebtedness (CIs) = public CIs and bills that are interest-bearing

data = [
    ("1941-Dec", 40000, 2002),
    ("1942-Jan", 42078, 2101),
    ("1942-Feb", 44305, 2002),
    ("1942-Mar", 44847, 1652),
    ("1942-Apr", 45360, 3460),
    ("1942-May", 48157, 3764),
    ("1942-Jun", 48776, 5604),
    ("1942-Jul", 51765, 6759),
    ("1942-Aug", 53680, 8873),
    ("1942-Sep", 54413, 10829),
    ("1942-Oct", 57285, 11336),
    ("1942-Nov", 57931, 12882),
    ("1942-Dec", 64868, 17161),
]

# Extract the two series
bonds = [d[1] for d in data]
bills = [d[2] for d in data]

print("Data points:")
for i, d in enumerate(data):
    print(f"{d[0]}: Bonds={d[1]}, Bills/CI={d[2]}")

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
n = len(bonds)
mean_bonds = sum(bonds) / n
mean_bills = sum(bills) / n

print(f"\nMean bonds: {mean_bonds}")
print(f"Mean bills: {mean_bills}")

# Calculate covariance
cov = sum((bonds[i] - mean_bonds) * (bills[i] - mean_bills) for i in range(n)) / n

# Calculate standard deviations
std_bonds = math.sqrt(sum((b - mean_bonds)**2 for b in bonds) / n)
std_bills = math.sqrt(sum((b - mean_bills)**2 for b in bills) / n)

print(f"Std bonds: {std_bonds}")
print(f"Std bills: {std_bills}")

# Pearson correlation
r = cov / (std_bonds * std_bills)
print(f"\nPearson correlation coefficient: {r}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(r, 3)}")
EOF
